thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p95/p99 latency SLO breach detected for /v1/generate (streaming) — sudden tail spike starting ~10:42 UTC. Pager routed to oncall-jay.

oncall-jay: looking now. seeing p95 ~ 850ms -> 3s and p99 ~ 7s. streaming stalls reported by customers.

maria: I can join, pulling traces and recent deploys. any deploys to prompt-preproc in last 30m?

kevin: yes, we shipped a change ~10:30 to JSON-mode coercion in prompt-preproc. It added a new parse pass to validate tool schemas. small change but carts into path for streaming.

jen: timeline: 10:30 deploy -> 10:38 first small uptick -> 10:42 paging. looks correlated.

oncall-jay: ok rollback plan? we can revert the extra parse pass or rate-limit the new code path.

kevin: quick mitigation: flip feature flag to bypass JSON-mode validation for streaming routes. flag name `preproc.skip_json_validation_streaming`.

oncall-jay: doing flip now.

incident-bot: ACTION: oncall-jay toggled preproc.skip_json_validation_streaming -> true (10:45:12 UTC)

maria: metrics updating — p95 down to ~600ms now. p99 still at ~2.5s. some streaming sessions still stall (observed stalls at token 0 -> no first-chunk).

kevin: that stall pattern looks like KV-cache warmup + the extra parse path hitting a sync lock. check tokenizer queue depth.

jen: pulling tokenizer-service metrics — queue depth spiked from 40 -> 420 around 10:40, worker CPU ~98% on one shard.

alex: Customer Impact: two customers reported degraded streaming (chatbots freezing) and one high-volume partner saw 12% request error-like behavior (timeouts). No data loss.

elena: creating an incident page entry and marking P2 with customer-facing notices. draft status now.

maria: looking at logs. saw repeated lines:

```
WARN preproc: json_coerce: schema_check_blocking=true id=abcd-1234 duration_ms=1200
ERROR tokenizer: read_timeout after 5000ms id=abcd-1234
```

maria: the `schema_check_blocking=true` flag came from the new code path. it's synchronous for streaming requests when schema contains `additionalProperties: false`.

kevin: rough root cause: prompt templates with nested tool schemas triggered expensive JSON validation in-line with tokenization, which serialized across requests on the single validation worker. combination of heavier templates + burst traffic = blocking queue.

oncall-jay: mitigation path: 1) keep skip_json_validation_streaming=true, 2) increase preproc validation worker pool from 2 -> 6 on the shard, 3) add async validation for future runs, 4) roll back the schema coercion change if not safe.

jen: I'm bumping workers now for the affected pool.

incident-bot: ACTION: eng-runtime autoscaler updated `preproc-validation-pool` desired=6 (10:53:07 UTC)

maria: after worker bump p95 ~ 220ms, p99 ~ 720ms. stalls dropping.

kevin: I'll open a revert PR for the JSON-mode coercion and add tests for async validation with streaming. tagging @devex for prompt template guidance.

jen: we should also add a hotfix: short-circuit validation for templates with more than N tokens or containing tool schemas that are flagged expensive. config param `preproc.max_sync_schema_tokens=256`.

elena: status page: posted update — "Investigating: streaming latency impact for /v1/generate. Mitigation in progress; temporary bypass enabled. We will update in 30 minutes."

alex: support notes: advise affected customers to expect intermittent small delays, we have feature flag bypass in place and worker scaling applied. open ticket for partners with higher SLA.

oncall-jay: handoff to maria for night oncall. I'll stay on slack for 15m for questions.

maria: taking over. next steps: validate reduced error-rate for 2h, merge revert + async validation, add regression test to CI to simulate heavy nested tool schema.

kevin: PR created: r/infra#5123 (revert + async path), adding perf test harness for nested tool schemas + streaming.

maria: postmortem notes to capture: root cause, template schema validation in the hot path, insufficient validation worker capacity, lack of regression test for streaming+tool-schemas, and follow-ups: a) make schema validation async by default for streaming, b) add preproc throttling/circuit-breaker, c) add traffic-driven autoscaling rule for validation pool.

elena: assigning postmortem owners: maria (write), kevin (fix), jen (deployment safety), elena (customer comms).

incident-bot: INCIDENT: state=mitigated (10:57:32 UTC) — p95/p99 under SLOs, customer reports improving.

maria: thanks team. I'll file the postmortem draft and ping here when ready. :white_check_mark:
